purpose: Define a Domain as an explicit semantic composition identity over Universal Modules, primitives, relations and domain-specific rules without becoming a replacement owner of its substrates.

topics.name: Domain Identity
topics.purpose: Define a Domain as an explicit semantic composition identity over Universal Modules, primitives, relations and domain-specific rules without becoming a replacement owner of its substrates.

semantics.identity_rule: Each Domain has an explicit stable identity.
semantics.composition_rule: Domain references exact Universal Module/primitive/relation identities.
semantics.ownership_rule: Domain owns only its composition/domain-specific semantics.
semantics.substrate_rule: Underlying Universal Modules retain primitive ownership.
semantics.instance_rule: Domain definition and concrete domain instance/context are separate.
semantics.authority_rule: Domain membership grants no runtime authority.

invariants.rule: Composition never silently transfers semantic ownership: universal modules own their primitives, domains own their composition semantics, and composed members retain their own identities and contracts.

Containment, relation, dependency, composition and projection edges exist only through explicit typed references; naming, file hierarchy, UI adjacency or shared values never create semantic structure.

hard_gates.condition: domain copies modules and takes ownership
same modules imply same domain automatically
